{"candidate_rtl":"module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
wire [63:0] add_a = Oper[1] ? ~a : a;
wire [63:0] add_b = Oper[0] ? ~b : b;
wire add_cin = Oper[1] | Oper[0];
wire [63:0] arithmetic_sum = add_a + add_b + add_cin;

always @(*) begin
    case (Oper)
        3'b000, 3'b001, 3'b010: sum = arithmetic_sum;
        3'b011: sum = a | b;
        3'b100: sum = a & b;
        3'b101: sum = a ^ b;
        3'b110: sum = a ~^ b;
        default: sum = 64'b0;
    endcase
end
endmodule","bottleneck":"The dominant path is the 64-bit arithmetic result, including operation-dependent operand inversion, carry-in selection, and the final carry-propagation network. The original implementation also exposes a 65-bit concatenated arithmetic assignment and allows separate add/subtract structures before selection.","rewrite":"Share one 64-bit adder for all three arithmetic operations by conditionally complementing a and b and using Oper[1]|Oper[0] as the two's-complement carry-in. Keep the four logic operations and default case as direct result selections, while omitting the unobservable c_out.","expected_timing_gain":"Expected lower maximum data arrival from eliminating duplicated arithmetic-selection structure and reducing arithmetic width to the observed 64-bit result. The exact gain depends on Yosys/ABC factoring and cell mapping; no timing value is guaranteed.","area_or_other_cost":"Likely reduced or comparable area because one arithmetic datapath is shared and the unobservable carry output is removed. Conditional inversion and the result mux remain, with no added storage or buffering.","functional_boundaries":"For Oper=000, 001, and 010, arithmetic_sum produces the low 64 bits of a+b, a-b, and b-a respectively; carry-out is intentionally unobservable. Oper=011,100,101,110 produce OR, AND, XOR, and XNOR. All other Oper values produce 64'b0. Inputs are treated as unsigned 64-bit vectors, and all outputs match the original for every binary input."}
